economy.summary: His campaign says Northeastern Pennsylvania families are hurting from high costs and calls for stopping reckless federal spending, getting inflation under control, and cutting taxes.
economy.short: Calls for stopping reckless spending, controlling inflation, cutting taxes.

taxes.summary: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in 2025 and said its tax cuts are a win for working families and middle-class America, citing a doubled Child Tax Credit, no taxes on tips or overtime, and additional tax relief for seniors.
taxes.short: Voted for 2025 tax law; says cuts help working families.

abortion.summary: Said in an October 2024 debate that he would not support a federal ban on abortion under any circumstances, and that state voters should decide the issue through ballot measures rather than federal representatives.
abortion.short: Opposes federal abortion ban; says state voters should decide.

education.summary: Said he supports school choice, telling a radio interviewer that he personally feels the dollar should follow the child to the school a family chooses.
education.short: Supports school choice; says dollars should follow the child.

healthcare.summary: Says the 2025 reconciliation law protects Medicaid while rooting out waste, supports its 20-hour-per-week work requirement, and says he negotiated to block proposals to lower the Medicaid provider tax; also pledges to oppose raising the retirement age or cutting Social Security and Medicare benefits.
healthcare.short: Says Medicaid protected; supports work requirements; opposes benefit cuts.

energy.summary: Celebrated Blackstone's planned $25 billion investment in new natural gas power plants in Northeastern Pennsylvania, saying it will bring thousands of family-sustaining jobs, and has discussed lifting the Delaware River Basin Commission's fracking ban to expand gas development.
energy.short: Supports expanding natural gas plants and regional gas development.

guns.summary: His campaign says he stands with law enforcement and will ensure police have the resources to combat the fentanyl crisis, citing his past donations and support for local police.
guns.short: Pledges to stand with law enforcement; fund fentanyl fight.

economy.summary: Her campaign platform proposes breaking up monopolies she says hurt small businesses and raise costs, capping credit card fees, strengthening unions, and reshoring manufacturing jobs, including more defense manufacturing in Northeastern Pennsylvania.
economy.short: Proposes breaking up monopolies, capping fees, reshoring manufacturing jobs.

taxes.summary: Criticized the 2025 tax-and-spending law, saying it cut roughly $1 trillion from Medicaid to fund tax cuts for billionaires, and said broad tariffs are spiking the cost of groceries and housing; her platform opposes broad tariffs while supporting targeted tariffs to protect manufacturing.
taxes.short: Opposes 2025 tax law and broad tariffs; supports targeted tariffs.

abortion.summary: Is endorsed for the 2026 race by Reproductive Freedom for All and EMILYs List, organizations that endorse candidates who support abortion rights; her campaign site does not detail an abortion platform.
abortion.short: Endorsed by groups that back candidates supporting abortion rights.

healthcare.summary: Her platform proposes preventing healthcare industry middlemen from denying care and medications prescribed by doctors and reforming insurance so coverage protects people; she opposes the 2025 law's Medicaid cuts, saying they could take health care away from more than 30,000 people in the district.
healthcare.short: Proposes stopping middlemen denying care; opposes Medicaid cuts.

guns.summary: Says she plans to work to implement universal background checks on gun sales nationwide and strengthen safe storage measures while respecting the rights of gun owners; as mayor she established Scranton's first community violence intervention and prevention program.
guns.short: Supports universal background checks, safe storage; respects gun owners.
